title: Molecular Insights into the Oxygen-Tolerant Dissimilatory Nitrate Reduction to Ammonium by Sulfide Oxidation in Mycobacterium.
authors: Jia, Tipei; Peng, Yongzhen; Niu, Lishan; Qi, Zheng; Xi, Jinying
one_liner_zh: 该文通过转录组与分子动力学模拟研究分枝杆菌中NarGHI复合物的氧耐受DNRA机制，涉及蛋白-DNA互作（NarL调控）但非TF-DNA结合建模核心，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系。
abstract: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), essential for nitrogen retention in ecosystems, is traditionally considered a strictly anaerobic process. Challenging this, emerging evidence revealed robust DNRA activity under aerobic conditions, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. In this study, we elucidate the molecular basis of oxygen-tolerant DNRA driven by sulfide oxidation in a Mycobacterium-dominated system. Under fully aerobic conditions (dissolved oxygen >3 mg/L), this system converted 1.4-4.5 mmol of nitrate to ammonium per 100 mmol of sulfide oxidized, with efficiency increasing at higher sulfide loads. Transcriptomic analysis revealed strong upregulation of DNRA genes (narGHI, nirBD) in Mycobacterium in response to elevated sulfide. In contrast to canonical DNRA organisms, which rely on the oxygen-sensitive transcription factor Fnr, Mycobacterium lacks the fnr gene and instead uses the nitrite-responsive NarL to drive DNRA gene expression irrespective of oxygen availability. Structural and molecular-dynamics analysis of Mycobacterium NarGHI complex horizontal line initiating enzyme of DNRA horizontal line reveals an evolutionarily adapted, distinctly narrowed, and highly hydrophobic substrate channel. This confined architecture protects the catalytic site from oxidative damage by raising the O(2) diffusion free-energy barrier and enhancing nitrate-specific induced-fit recognition. Our findings reveal metabolic plasticity of microbial nitrogen cycling, imply convergent evolutionary strategies for oxygen tolerance in other classically anaerobic pathways, and offer key practical insights for optimizing nitrogen management in both sustainable agriculture and wastewater treatment.
abstract_zh: 异化硝酸盐还原为铵（DNRA）是生态系统中氮保留的关键过程，传统上被认为是一种严格厌氧的代谢途径。然而，新出现的证据表明，在有氧条件下DNRA活性依然显著，但其潜在机制尚不明确。在本研究中，我们阐明了以分枝杆菌（Mycobacterium）为主导的系统中，由硫化物氧化驱动的耐氧DNRA的分子基础。在完全有氧条件下（溶解氧>3 mg/L），该系统每氧化100 mmol硫化物可将1.4–4.5 mmol硝酸盐转化为铵，且效率随硫化物负荷升高而增加。转录组分析显示，分枝杆菌中DNRA基因（narGHI、nirBD）在硫化物升高时显著上调。与依赖氧敏感转录因子Fnr的典型DNRA生物不同，分枝杆菌缺乏fnr基因，而是利用亚硝酸盐响应的NarL来驱动DNRA基因表达，且不受氧气可用性影响。对分枝杆菌NarGHI复合物（DNRA起始酶）的结构和分子动力学分析揭示了一个进化适应性的、显著狭窄且高度疏水的底物通道。这种受限结构通过提高O(2)扩散自由能屏障并增强硝酸盐特异性诱导契合识别，保护催化位点免受氧化损伤。我们的发现揭示了微生物氮循环的代谢可塑性，暗示了其他经典厌氧途径中耐氧策略的趋同进化，并为优化可持续农业和废水处理中的氮管理提供了关键实践见解。
